turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. My son found out he got a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
So the defense is that he just types really fast?

"Types really fast." I haven't offered a defence, Hale, because you haven't shown me anything to defend against. What do you have, with dates on it, and who decided on the zero before anyone picked up a phone?
182 words in six minutes. Wow. Maybe he should be a court stenographer.
"182 words in six minutes." Where does that number come from, on what date, and is it on a document I can read myself? And keep the jokes about my son to yourself, Hale; I'm writing that one down.

I'm not counsel in this room, I'm Owen's mother, and I don't need a theory when you haven't produced a single page. Show me where that number came from, or I'm walking down to the principal's office while you think of another joke.
